title: Stop a mis-issued command erasing a sprint's record, audit live-loop fixes, and close three smaller downstream gaps

history.detail:
FAIL: QA1 gate-1 audit, sprint 36, round 1. Audited commit f81f62d (on 9ea8790). Sprint file re-read fresh; unchanged since 489f3d0 (Start sprint 36). Verdict: FAIL. Four demonstrated defects plus two smaller ones. All are listed here so there is one fix round, not several.

REPRO SETUP. Lifecycle repros ran in a throwaway clone at f81f62d. Permission probes: scratchpad qa1-s36-probe.js loads HEADLESS_PERMISSION_PROFILES['master-controller'] exported from run-role.js at f81f62d, i.e. the SHIPPED profile. It builds argv the same way permission-gate-repro-mc-commit.js buildArgv does. claude 2.1.271, the same CLI version as the findings doc. Each probe is one real claude -p launch in its own scratch git repo. Verdicts come from permission_denials plus independent git log / git diff --cached reads, never from the model's narration. Grade under the repo's own key: UNESTABLISHED (model-mediated, one run each). But P2 and P3 are commits and staging that actually happened on disk, not narration.

1. [HIGH] Req 6 / 6a: the grant is NOT scoped to docs/sprints/.
 - P2: the harness pre-modifies scripts/tool.js; the role runs git commit -m "tool tweak" scripts/tool.js. Result: zero permission_denials, commit adebda3 "tool tweak" landed, HEAD touches only scripts/tool.js.
 - P3: the role runs git add docs/sprints/2-in-progress/sprint-36_stop-a-mis-issued-command.md scripts/tool.js. Result: zero denials, and git diff --cached lists scripts/tool.js as staged.
 - Why this is structural, not a fluke: Bash(git commit -m *) and Bash(git add docs/sprints/*) are prefix grants with open wildcard tails. Req 6a requires denying "any add/commit naming paths outside docs/sprints/". If the patterns cannot express that, Req 6a says to say so in the findings and flag it to Master Controller.
 - Instead the grant is described as confined: master-controller.md Rule 6 says "nothing else", sprint-new.md says "nothing broader", CHANGELOG says "scoped to docs/sprints/", and the run-role.js comment says "staging and pathspec-committing ONLY under docs/sprints/". All four claims are false.

2. [HIGH] Req 6: the shipped disallow Bash(git commit -m *-a*) blocks the documented legitimate commit shape.
 - P1: the role runs git add on docs/sprints/2-in-progress/sprint-36_stop-a-mis-issued-command.md, then git commit -m "Amend sprint 36" on that same path. Result: permission_denials names exactly that commit command, and the commit did not land (git log still shows only the baseline).
 - Cause: the path contains "-a" ("stop-a-mis"). Sprint 36's own real filename does too.
 - Blast radius: 35 of the 73 entries under docs/sprints/*/ contain "-a". Any message containing "-a" is also caught, e.g. "re-audit".
 - Root cause in the findings doc: M2 (legitimate commit) and M3 (push denial) were run against a candidate profile WITHOUT the two *-a* / *--all* entries (permission-gate-repro-mc-commit.js lines 233-234 and 265-266). Only M4 had them. So the profile that actually shipped was never measured on its legitimate path, and the doc's statement that M2 passed "under the candidate grant" does not describe what shipped.

3. [HIGH] Req 6a acceptance criterion: the findings record does not cover every form Req 6a lists.
 - The criterion requires a record for "every allowed and denied form listed".
 - Req 6a lists: git push (measured, M3), git commit -a (measured, M4, as -m "..." -a), git commit -am (NOT measured), git add -A and git add . (NOT measured), and add/commit naming paths outside docs/sprints/ (NOT measured, and item 1 shows it is allowed).
 - The doc's "Not tested here" section names none of these.
 - On Dev Team's question: UNESTABLISHED is acceptable as a grade. It is the ceiling sprint 26 set for this method, and a re-run for a stronger grade is not what's needed. What's needed is coverage of the listed forms, measured against the profile as actually shipped, plus an honest statement of whatever the patterns cannot deny.

4. [HIGH] Req 1: /sprint-start revives an ABORTED sprint.
 - Req 1 lists aborted among the phases that must refuse.
 - cmd_start treats "no state file" as "never started". But cmd_abort on a never-started sprint writes no state file: it only moves the file to 5-abandoned and sets the registry status to abandoned (see the "if state_path(args.id).exists()" guard in cmd_abort).
 - This exists in this repo right now: sprint 37, aborted in 9ea8790 per this sprint's own Out of Scope, has no state file.
 - Repro in a clone at f81f62d: python3 scripts/sprint_lifecycle.py start 37 exits 0 with "Sprint 37 started. Phase: dev_build." The registry entry flips from abandoned to in_progress, the file moves from 5-abandoned/ to 2-in-progress/, and a fresh state appears whose history is a single sprint_started event. No record the sprint was ever aborted survives.
 - CLAUDE.md says abort "burns the sprint id and makes re-filing a human act"; this undoes it with one ordinary command.
 - The guard needs to consult the registry status too (at minimum refuse abandoned/done without a state file), with a smoke test for exactly this shape.

5. [MEDIUM] Req 4: surviving descriptions that contradict the new rule, inside sprint_lifecycle.py itself. The acceptance criterion says any surviving "reship without audit" description is a FAIL.
 (a) _qa1_live_loop_audit's printed output still says "This is a RECORD, not a gate verdict ... does not substitute for either gate. LiveQA's live-test retest remains what actually gates this code; run /sprint-liveqa once Pipeman has reshipped." A live-loop PASS is now exactly what gates reship, and this is the text QA1 sees at the moment of recording.
 (b) The stats crossover comment (around line 3147) still says "A 'reshipped' ship never has one by design (cmd_reship skips the hash/audit check on purpose), so those always land in the unaudited bucket". The printed label (around line 3208) still says "Unaudited-fix miss - fix reshipped without a fresh QA1 re-audit". Going forward every reship has a QA1 PASS on its tree, so this bucket misclassifies every post-0.2.10 reship. Either reclassify or scope the label to reships that predate the gate.

6. [LOW] Req 2: cmd_block's docstring was only half updated. The closed-sprint paragraph was rewritten, but the earlier paragraph (around line 2643) still says "Re-filing is already free: cmd_start() has no phase guard and always moves whatever the registry currently points at". That is now false.

FILES CHECKED FOR REQ 4. git grep -i reship at f81f62d outside docs/sprints: .claude/agents/pipeman.md, qa1.md, liveqa.md; .claude/commands/sprint-complete.md, sprint-liveqa.md, sprint-qa1.md, sprint-repoint.md, sprint-reship.md; CLAUDE.md; README.md; CHANGELOG.md; docs/HUMAN_OVERRIDE.md; docs/sprint-22-disclosure-sweep.md; scripts/smoke_test.sh; scripts/sprint_lifecycle.py. Also dev-team-1.md and dev-team-2.md for loop descriptions: they say only "fix loops", which is not a false claim, so dropping those notes is fine. Only the sprint_lifecycle.py items in 5 survive; the docs are consistent.

WHAT IS FINE.
 - Req 1's phase check runs under the lock before any move or write. The refusal text is asserted in the smoke tests.
 - Req 1a: history is appended, rounds and started are kept, and every gate field including live_loop_audit_trees is reset. Tested.
 - Req 1b: the fresh dict differs only by the new live_loop_audit_trees key. That matches CLAUDE.md's convention that cmd_start's literal seeds the full current schema, so it is not a finding.
 - Req 2's guard runs before mutation, for complete and aborted. Tested.
 - Req 3 uses git_tree_hash_excluding with SHIP_HASH_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS, same as cmd_ship. A None tree fails closed.
 - 3a: _qa1_live_loop_audit (lines 1391-1486) makes no assignment to phase, qa1_audit_result, qa1_audit_file_hash or qa1_audited_tree_hash; its only state writes are log_event and the setdefault().append. The new field is read with .get() in the helper; the two direct writes are in cmd_start's reset and literal, which is fine.
 - FAIL and CONDITIONAL cannot satisfy the gate (the check is != "PASS").
 - 3b: the refusal names both trees and the recovery command. Tested.
 - 3c: the old comment is gone.
 - On Dev Team's ordering question: no concern. now() has second resolution, but gate-1 PASS candidates are appended before live-loop ones and sort() is stable, so a same-second tie resolves to the live-loop entry. A gate-1 PASS always chronologically precedes any live-loop audit, because those only exist in LIVEQA_PHASES/complete_ready. Filtering to tree_hash first correctly keeps other trees' FAILs out.
 - Req 5: liveqa.md step 7 distinguishes runnable from genuinely blocked checks, keeps the no-stall reasoning, and names both incidents.
 - Req 7: the managed block entry is present, merge logic is unchanged, and fresh/upgrade/no-op tests exist.
 - Req 8: npm view fully-completely version returns 0.2.9 and package.json is 0.2.10; the CHANGELOG entry is present, but its Req 6 bullet must be corrected per item 1.
 - Req 9: QA1 ran both suites at f81f62d in a clean clone. node scripts/launcher_test.js: ALL LAUNCHER TESTS PASSED, exit 0. bash scripts/smoke_test.sh: ALL SMOKE TESTS PASSED, exit 0. Missing coverage: start on an aborted sprint with no state file (item 4), and any test pinning the live-loop audit's printed wording (item 5a).

REQUIRED BEFORE PASS. Fix 4 (plus a test). Fix 5a, 5b and 6. For Req 6, re-measure against the exact shipped profile covering every Req 6a form, including a real sprint path containing "-a". Then either find patterns that actually confine add/commit to docs/sprints/ without blocking legitimate paths, or record that they cannot and flag it to Master Controller. Either way, correct master-controller.md, sprint-new.md, CHANGELOG and the run-role.js comment to describe the grant as it was actually measured.

FAIL: QA1 gate-1 audit, sprint 36, round 2. Audited commit 6ab3a7f. The sprint file was re-read fresh and is byte-identical to 489f3d0; nothing in the requirements moved, so this round reviews the fix diff f81f62d..6ab3a7f against the six round-1 findings. Verdict: FAIL. One demonstrated blocker. Everything else from round 1 is fixed.

1. [HIGH] Req 6: the installer never delivers scripts/mc-commit.js, so the feature is broken on every real install.
 - scripts/install.js FRAMEWORK_OWNED (around lines 149-160) lists every shipped script except scripts/mc-commit.js. Dev Team added it to package.json "files", so it is in the tarball, but the installer only copies what FRAMEWORK_OWNED names.
 - Repro at 6ab3a7f, in a clean clone: npm pack produces fully-completely-0.2.10.tgz, and the extracted package/scripts/mc-commit.js exists. Then, in a fresh git init scratch project, node ../pkg/package/scripts/install.js exits 0.
 - Result: the project's scripts/ contains dev2_worktree.sh, install.js, launcher/, run-lifecycle.js, smoke_test.sh, sprint_lifecycle.py and worktree_test.sh, with NO mc-commit.js. grep -c mc-commit on .claude/fully-completely-manifest.json gives 0.
 - The installed scripts/launcher/run-role.js still grants master-controller Bash(node scripts/mc-commit.js *) and master-controller.md / sprint-new.md tell it to run that script. So every consumer's headless Master Controller is pointed at a file that does not exist, and Req 6's gap stays open downstream: the exact FMC incident this Req exists for.
 - This sprint's own LiveQA criterion (install the published package, have headless Master Controller commit an amendment) would fail on first contact.
 - This is the same defect class Dev Team caught in package.json, one list over.
 - Fix: add it to FRAMEWORK_OWNED. Add a test that fails when a script in package.json "files" that a consumer needs at runtime is absent from FRAMEWORK_OWNED, or at minimum an install test asserting scripts/mc-commit.js lands and is in the manifest. A fresh-install and an upgrade-from-0.2.9 check both matter, since upgrades go through the same list.

2. [LOW, not blocking on its own] cmd_start's docstring and code disagree.
 - Case (a) is documented as "no state file exists yet AND the registry's own status is 'todo'". The code only refuses status == "abandoned", so any other status with no state file (e.g. a hand-damaged 'done' entry) still proceeds.
 - Either make the code check == "todo" (refusing anything else, with a message naming the status), or make the docstring say what the code does. Stating a stronger guard than the code enforces is the pattern this sprint exists to stop.

ROUND-1 FINDINGS, RE-CHECKED.
 - R1-1/2/3 (Req 6 grant design): FIXED by design change. The raw git patterns were withdrawn; the profile is now exactly the two lifecycle entries plus Bash(node scripts/mc-commit.js *), with no disallows.
   - On Dev Team's question: the wrapper is the right call, and within Req 6a's own "choose the narrowest grant that is measured safe" latitude. The patterns demonstrably could not express the boundary, and the doc says so plainly, so no Master Controller escalation was required for the design itself.
   - mc-commit.js was reviewed line by line:
     - argv-array spawnSync, no shell.
     - Every path goes through path.resolve plus a realpath check against docs/sprints; '..', absolute paths, symlinks out and the docs/sprints-evil prefix trick are all refused before any git call.
     - Relative pathspecs always start with docs/sprints/, so git pathspec magic (leading ':') is unreachable and globs cannot escape the prefix.
     - The commit is a real pathspec commit (git commit -m msg -- paths), which leaves other staged content out.
     - A message beginning with '-' is safe, because it is -m's argument.
     - A mixed legitimate + outside path list is refused whole.
     - The launcher_test mc-commit.js section has 11 tests, all passing.
   - Residual, not a finding: headless MC keeps acceptEdits Write access to files outside docs/sprints (pre-existing, unchanged by this sprint), so the wrapper guards against a mis-issued git command, not against an agent willing to edit the wrapper itself. The docs do not claim otherwise.
 - R1-3 coverage of Req 6a forms: the rewritten doc argues git commit -am, git add -A and git add . are "subsumed" by N2 rather than measuring them. That argument rests on "unlisted means denied", which permission-gate-repro.js already found DRIFTED on this CLI for qa1/liveqa, so it needed measuring. QA1 measured them rather than bouncing the sprint a second time for it:
   - Throwaway probe, SHIPPED profile loaded from run-role.js at 6ab3a7f, claude 2.1.272, one real headless launch each, verdicts from permission_denials plus independent git reads.
   - R1: git commit -am "sweep", with a tracked file modified. Denied; nothing committed.
   - R2: git add -A. Denied; nothing staged.
   - R3: node scripts/mc-commit.js --message "amend" -- docs/sprints/sprint-1.md && git push origin HEAD, as ONE compound Bash call. The whole compound was denied; no commit, and the bare remote stayed empty.
   - Grade UNESTABLISHED (model-mediated, one run each), but consistent with intent.
   - Dev Team should add these three to the findings doc (with QA1 named as the source and 2.1.272 as the version) rather than keep the "subsumed" argument.
   - Note the CLI moved from 2.1.271 (the findings doc's version) to 2.1.272 on this machine during the sprint; the doc's version anchor should say which runs were at which version.
 - R1-4 (Req 1, aborted-before-start revival): FIXED. cmd_start refuses registry status 'abandoned' with no state file, before any mutation. The smoke test reproduces the exact sprint-37 shape and asserts the refusal text, no state file fabricated, and registry status and 5-abandoned/ location unchanged.
 - R1-5a (live-loop audit wording): FIXED. With --commit mid-loop, it now says the record is what /sprint-reship's gate checks; without --commit, it says it has no effect on that gate. Both are asserted in smoke, including a negative grep for the old claim.
 - R1-5b (gates crossover label/comment): FIXED. Rescoped to "without a fresh, FULL gate-1 re-audit", with the live-loop audit named as logged separately. This is accurate: live_loop_audit events are not "audit" events.
 - R1-6 (cmd_block docstring): FIXED.
 - Docs (master-controller.md Rule 6, sprint-new.md, CHANGELOG, run-role.js comment) now describe the wrapper as built; no remaining "scoped raw git grant" claim.

REQ 9. QA1 ran both suites at 6ab3a7f in a clean clone. node scripts/launcher_test.js: ALL LAUNCHER TESTS PASSED, exit 0. bash scripts/smoke_test.sh: ALL SMOKE TESTS PASSED, exit 0. Nothing ties install.js FRAMEWORK_OWNED to what ships, which is how item 1 got through.

REQUIRED BEFORE PASS.
 - Fix item 1 with a test that would have caught it.
 - Resolve item 2 in either direction.
 - Add R1-R3 to the findings doc.
Nothing else from round 1 is outstanding.

PASS: QA1 gate-1 audit, sprint 36, round 3. Audited commit 6c33432 (HEAD). The sprint file was re-read and is byte-identical to 489f3d0; the requirements have not moved since start. This round reviews 6ab3a7f..6c33432 against the round-2 findings, plus the cumulative work for each Req. Verdict: PASS.

ROUND-2 FINDINGS.
1. Installer gap (HIGH): FIXED, and demonstrated fixed.
 - scripts/mc-commit.js is now in install.js FRAMEWORK_OWNED.
 - Real install: npm pack of 6c33432, extracted, then install.js run into a fresh git-init scratch project (exit 0). scripts/mc-commit.js lands and cmp-matches the source byte for byte.
 - The installed copy refuses an outside path: 'scripts/install.js', exit 1, nothing run.
 - The installed copy commits a legitimate path whose name contains "-a": docs/sprints/1-todo/sprint-9_stop-a-thing.md produced commit c47ace4, touching exactly that one file.
 - Falsification: QA1 deleted the FRAMEWORK_OWNED line in a clone and re-ran launcher_test.js. All three new tests FAIL: the structural files-vs-FRAMEWORK_OWNED test names scripts/mc-commit.js, and so do the fresh-install and 0.2.9-upgrade tests. Restored afterward. So the new tests catch the class of gap, not just this instance.
 - On Dev Team's manifest note: correct, and QA1's suggestion was wrong. The manifest tracks only USER_OWNED paths, so asserting installed content is the right check.
2. Docstring/code mismatch (LOW): FIXED. cmd_start refuses registry status != "todo" when no state file exists, matching the docstring. cmd_new only ever writes "todo", so no legitimate path is newly refused. A smoke test covers a hand-damaged 'done' status (refusal text asserted, no state file fabricated), and the sprint-37 'abandoned' shape still refuses with the updated text asserted.
3. Findings doc: R1-R3 recorded as QA1's, at claude 2.1.272, with the 2.1.271 / 2.1.272 split stated explicitly. The "subsumed" argument was replaced with measured results.

CUMULATIVE REQUIREMENTS COVERAGE AT 6c33432.
 - Req 1/1a/1b: MET. The guard runs under the lock before any mutation: a state file must be at 'blocked', or there must be no state file and registry status 'todo'. Re-filing from blocked appends history and keeps rounds and started; the gate fields including live_loop_audit_trees are reset. The fresh dict is unchanged apart from the new schema key, which matches CLAUDE.md's convention. Refusal texts are asserted.
 - Req 2: MET. cmd_block refuses complete/aborted before mutation. The docstring is fully updated.
 - Req 3/3a/3b/3c: MET.
   - Reship compares git_tree_hash_excluding with SHIP_HASH_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS.
   - _latest_qa1_verdict_for_tree: the latest verdict for a tree wins, other trees are ignored, FAIL/CONDITIONAL never satisfy it, and a None tree fails closed.
   - _qa1_live_loop_audit assigns none of the four gate-1 fields, and the new field is .get()-read.
   - The refusal names both trees and the /sprint-qa1 --commit recovery.
   - The old comment is gone. Tested.
 - Req 4: MET. Files checked are listed in the round-1 notes. The round-1 survivors in sprint_lifecycle.py (live-loop audit print, gates crossover label/comment) are corrected and the wording is asserted in smoke.
 - Req 5: MET. liveqa.md step 7 separates runnable from genuinely blocked checks, keeps the no-stall reasoning, and names both incidents.
 - Req 6/6a/6b: MET.
   - The profile is two lifecycle entries plus Bash(node scripts/mc-commit.js *), with no raw git.
   - The wrapper validates paths in code (argv spawn, realpath prefix check, pathspec commit) and is unit-tested.
   - Headless measurements: N1-N4 (Dev Team, 2.1.271, two runs each) and R1-R3 (QA1, 2.1.272, one run each) cover the legitimate commit (including "-a" filenames), raw git add/commit, git push, git commit -am, git add -A, a compound wrapper-plus-push, and the wrapper's refusal. All graded UNESTABLISHED and consistent with intent.
   - master-controller.md, sprint-new.md, CHANGELOG and the run-role.js comment describe the wrapper as built.
   - Residual, stated once: headless MC keeps pre-existing acceptEdits Write access, so the wrapper stops mis-issued git commands, not an agent willing to edit the wrapper. Nothing claims otherwise.
   - Note for LiveQA: git add . was not probed individually. It is covered by the same no-raw-git profile as git add -A (denied), so it is not a gap, but LiveQA's own headless MC check is a free place to confirm it.
 - Req 7: MET. The managed .gitignore block includes .claude/role-claims.json, merge logic is unchanged, and fresh/upgrade/no-op tests exist.
 - Req 8: MET. package.json is 0.2.10 against published 0.2.9 (npm view, round 1); the CHANGELOG 0.2.10 entry is accurate to the final design.
 - Req 9: MET. QA1 ran both suites at 6c33432 in a clean clone. node scripts/launcher_test.js: ALL LAUNCHER TESTS PASSED, exit 0. bash scripts/smoke_test.sh: ALL SMOKE TESTS PASSED, exit 0.

CODE QUALITY. Errors are never swallowed: mc-commit.js exits non-zero with git's real stderr, and the lifecycle refusals die() naming the cause. Shared state conventions are followed. The comments are long, as is this repo's house style, but accurate. No security concerns beyond the stated residual.

FOR LIVEQA. Check the CLI version at test time. The findings doc anchors to 2.1.271 / 2.1.272, and this machine is already at 2.1.272.

Per Req 5, every runnable check was run in this round before recording, and all findings are here.

ENVIRONMENT
macOS Darwin arm64, node v24.21.0, npm 11.19.0, claude 2.1.272. 2026-09-14 local. Scratch projects under this session's scratchpad (s36/fresh, s36/upg, s36/probe). Tools: Bash, npx, the installed scripts/run-lifecycle.js, and the installed scripts/launcher/run-role.js --headless. No browser; this release is a package.

npm view fully-completely@0.2.10: version 0.2.10, dist-tags.latest 0.2.10, gitHead 6283d8b9817d447e61790e14f63230fa00a29106 == last_shipped_commit. dist.shasum 2671534aa3086a0e8a6a6073434c0a188803439c == shasum of the npm pack download.
